transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-29
- Time: 16:00 UTC (Zoom)
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Carlos (CSM), Rachel, Tom, Nina, Arjun (Meridian)

Summary: quick discovery to map Meridian Trust's requirements around logging, PII redaction, data residency and whether Hosted / Dedicated / Private makes sense. Customer wants an ops playbook for audits and a clear path for log redaction and key residency.

Topics: scope of logs captured, ability to disable or redact logs, KMS / HSM integration, cross-border log replication, SOC2/ISO evidence, HIPAA/financial controls, pilot runway and timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick intro - im Maya, AE at Redwood. the idea today is to understand what Meridian needs for logs and retention so we can propose the right deployment - hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:12] Rachel: hey, Rachel here. we run custodial trust accounts, so audit trails and proof of non-exfiltration are huge for us. primary question — can you avoid logging PII or redact it on ingestion? and also who can access those logs?
[00:26] Liam: great question. short answer is yes, we have multiple levers — configurable logging levels, on-ingest redaction hooks, and optional private deployment options where logs never leave the VPC. that said we should map your exact payloads to validate rules.
[00:40] Tom: when you say "on-ingest redaction hooks" is that something we run in our infra or inside Redwood? latency impact?
[00:50] Liam: two modes — one, pre-processing inside your pipeline (your side) before we see the text; two, if you want Redwood to handle it we can run redaction in the private plane or dedicated instances with customer-provided KMS. latency is minimal for token-masking rules, we measured typical add of 10-30ms per request depending on complexity.
[01:05] Rachel: we can't have PII in logs for EU customers. GDPR concerns. Also HIPAA for some account classes. can you show separation by jurisdiction?
[01:16] Maya: yes, region-locking is available — you can pin inference to eu-west and we can disable cross-region log replication for that tenant. for HIPAA, our Private deployment option supports on-prem or VPC-only telemetry retention policies.
[01:30] Nina: quick clarifying q: if we use hosted and ask to disable logging, does Redwood still keep any metadata for billing/usage? we need minimal footprint for compliance.
[01:43] Carlos: i'm Carlos from CS, folks often want usage metrics for billing but we support token-aggregates that are pseudonymized. we can also offer a custom contract to omit detailed payload-level logs for specific accounts.
[01:56] Arjun: what's the process for key management? we are required to use our KMS and have CMKs under our control.
[02:05] Liam: we have integration with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) — you can bring your own CMK for model encryption and disk-level encryption, plus HSM for private deployments if required. important caveat: some hosted features (like multi-tenant model caching) may require different architecture; we'll outline the tradeoffs in the proposal.
[02:26] Tom: ok tradeoffs = what exactly? if we choose hosted for speed and cost, do we lose the ability to fully control keys and logs?
[02:36] Maya: hosted is fastest to get started but you cede some control — for example full payload-level logs may be stored for debugging and incident response unless contractually disabled. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and more isolation, and Private gives the maximum control (VPC/on-prem) but longer lead time and ops ownership.
[02:54] Rachel: also results retention - we have a regulator asking for 7 years of audit trails for certain instruments. can Redwood retain encrypted audit logs for that long and provide an immutable export?
[03:06] Liam: yes, we can configure retention windows and immutable exports — we support write-once archival to object stores and can provide integrity proofs (hash chains) for exports. cost implications will differ.
[03:18] Nina: talking about masking, can you do selective redaction where certain fields are hashed and others removed? our legal wants pseudonymization not deletion for some datasets.
[03:29] Liam: absolutely. we have redaction templates — e.g., mask social security numbers with salted hashing, redact names, keep transaction ids. templates are configurable per-route so you can adjust per-instrument.
[03:41] Speaker 1: hm is there an SDK or plugin?
[03:44] Maya: yes, SDKs and a webhook for pre-processing. we also have a middleware library you can run in your infra before sending data to Redwood to minimize any PII hitting our plane.
[03:55] Rachel: i'd like to see the playbook for audits — steps you take when a regulator asks for proof: what logs you hand over, redaction, and chain-of-custody.
[04:06] Maya: good point. we'll share a sample ops playbook — includes log collection, retention, access controls, redaction policy, KMS audit trails, and how to run forensics in a private deployment.
[04:16] Tom: on access controls, is there RBAC/audit for Redwood employees? we need strict separation and recorded approvals for any human access to logs.
[04:25] Carlos: yes, Redwood enforces least privilege, just-in-time access, and every access request is logged. for enterprise contracts we can tie that to SSO/SAML and provide audit trails for admin approvals.
[04:37] Arjun: what about the ability to delete or purge logs for in-scope customers when required by regulation?
[04:44] Liam: we support programmatic retention policies and purge APIs. note that for immutable archives we produce an export and then we can terminate our copies if that's in the contract. the export can be delivered to your S3 with server-side encryption.
[04:59] Nina: can you offer a test where we simulate a SAR (subject access request) or an auditor request to see the end-to-end playbook?
[05:08] Maya: yes, part of pilot we can run a simulated audit. we'll include that in the scope doc.
[05:15] Tom: ok timeline question — we're aiming for a Q3 compliance window. what's the shortest runway for Private deployment?
[05:24] Liam: Private deployments take longer — typically 8-12 weeks for VPC onboarding + KMS/HSM validation + runbook testing. Dedicated is faster — usually 3-6 weeks to reserve capacity and set up isolations. hosted is immediate but with the constraints we discussed.
[05:38] Rachel: one more: vendor access — do you have personnel in other regions that could access EU logs? we need geo-fencing for human access too.
[05:46] Maya: yes, geo-fencing for human ops is available in Private and Dedicated; hosted will have centralized SRE ops but we can include contractual geo-restrictions for enterprise agreements — will need legal sign-off.
[05:58] Carlos: also want to flag logging of system prompts — some customers consider system prompts sensitive. you can configure to not log system-level prompts or to separate them with higher retention controls.
[06:09] Arjun: for the pilot, we'd prefer private with a small set of instances in our VPC to validate redaction and retention mechanics. can you run that as a proof-of-concept?
[06:18] Liam: yep; pilot options: 1) private in your cloud account (we run images you approve) 2) dedicated where we host in our infra but reserve nodes for you and set log exclusions 3) hosted with heavy contract controls. we'll draft configs for each.
[06:33] Rachel: send reference customers who've done similar work, esp financials.
[06:36] Maya: we'll share a short list — names and contactable folks under NDA if needed.
[06:41] Tom: any known limitations with ML eval / quality monitoring when we disable payload logging? we rely on that data to detect regressions.
[06:50] Liam: good point — if payload logs are disabled we offer a client-side eval shim: you can send anonymized hashes and selected metrics that let us run quality checks without raw text. also we can run deterministic evals in-private in your VPC.
[07:06] Speaker 2: (overlap) and token accounting?
[07:08] Carlos: accounting will still happen at token-aggregate level — for billing we can send aggregated daily totals. if you need per-invocation billing we can do that in dedicated/private with billing hooks into your systems.
[07:20] Nina: ok next steps hopefully include docs and a security deep dive.
[07:24] Maya: recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO pack, sample ops playbook, pilot configs for private + dedicated + hosted, cost estimates, and schedule a security deep-dive next week. action items noted.
[07:36] Rachel: thanks, appreciate quick turnaround.
[07:39] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc bundle.

End of transcript.

Notes on audio quality: automatic transcription has occasional mislabels (Speaker 1/2) and some OCR-like errors for product names; we left those as-is.
